summary: Two-story stone Vista House (1933) at the summit of Mount Spokane State Park; NRHP-listed 2018; the summit fire towers around it changed often, and the 1979 tower moved to Quartz Mountain.

facts.design: Two-story rustic stone building (1933) with a second-floor fire lookout room
facts.agency: Washington State Parks and Recreation Commission owns the stone building; the summit towers belong to the Department of Natural Resources (per NHLR)

access.note: A visitor building at the summit of Mount Spokane State Park; the Historic Spokane record describes it as serving the visiting public.

visit.trail_note: TrailChick: it is possible to drive very near the summit, except in spring when snow may remain on the road.

events.note: Two-story stone Vista House, completed November 21, 1933, as an emergency relief project; second-floor fire lookout room
Wooden summit tower. NHLR: live-in tower. TrailChick: 83 ft with 14x14 cab.
Summit tower collapsed under ice. NHLR: the first winter. TrailChick: a year later, in a February 15, 1949 storm.
TrailChick: 40-ft DNR tower replaced the 45-ft tower
NHLR: the 40-ft tower replaced the 1959 tower about 13 years later (year calculated from NHLR)
TrailChick: the 1979 summit tower stayed in service until 1994. This is the summit tower, not the stone building.
1979 summit tower moved to Quartz Mountain, where it still stands and rents overnight
Spokane Register listing. Historic Spokane's table gives April 16, 2019; its text gives June 3, 2019.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR calls it a live-in tower that collapsed the first winter. TrailChick says 83 ft with a 14x14 cab that collapsed a year later, in a February 1949 storm. The story uses only the points the sources share.
NHLR: a shorter tower built 1959, replaced about 13 years later. TrailChick: built 1950, replaced 1963. The 1979 date agrees across both sources.

NHLR (registered 1993) calls the 1979 tower still in service, which fits its registration date. TrailChick says it stayed in service until 1994, was dismantled in 2001, and was moved to Quartz Mountain in 2004.
Historic Spokane's record gives April 16, 2019 in its table and June 3, 2019 in its text.

TrailChick notes that some sources credit the CCC, but a state plan it cites credits local contractor E.O. Fieldstad. NHLR and the State Parks blog also name Fieldstad. SpokaneTalk spells the name Fieldstead.
Historic Spokane and TrailChick spell it Bertelsen; the State Parks blog spells it Bertlesen. The story uses Bertelsen.

notes_for_editor: The record is for the stone Vista House (NHLR). The summit fire towers are separate structures, and their dates conflict between NHLR (registered 1993) and TrailChick. The 1979 tower moved to Quartz Mountain in 2004; the existing us-wa-mount-spokane-at-quartz-mountain record Cross-checked with us-wa-mount-spokane-at-quartz-mountain on 2026-10-08: that record dates the Vista House to 1934 from TrailChick, while this record uses the State Parks 1933 date; it also attributes an 85-ft first-winter collapse to TrailChick, but TrailChick (source 4 here) gives 83 ft and a collapse a year later. Those points belong to the Quartz record's editor to reconcile; this story does not repeat them. I found no staffing data for the stone building, so no staffing fact is set. The brief's elevation of 1781.3 m matches NHLR's 5,844 ft for the building; TrailChick gives the summit as 5,883 ft and the State Parks blog gives the mountain as 5,887 ft. The brief's NRHP number 100003229 is confirmed by the NRHP date in Historic Spokane's record.
